subject: Clarify token packaging, context billing & minimums for DataAxis pilot
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@dataaxis.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataAxis Procurement <procurement@dataaxis.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot pricing questions — token accounting and minimums

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is reviewing the proposed SOW and we have a couple of technical billing questions to clear up before we run the internal approval:

1) How exactly are tokens counted for long-context calls that stream? If a customer uses a 40k-context request that streams partial outputs over 2 minutes, do we charge for full 40k tokens up front or per token produced/consumed?

2) Rounding/minimums: your sales engineer mentioned a 1k-token quantum and a 1-call minimum. We need an explicit example of how rounding behaves for brief calls and for many small requests (e.g., 120 requests of ~90 tokens).

3) Packaging/discounts: For a 3-month pilot (expected ~2M tokens/month but spiky), what packaging options should we consider? Committed token blocks vs per-token with an overage cap? Also curious if you offer pilot-specific pilot discounts or onboarding credits.

I've attached the draft SOW (DataAxis_SOW_v1.pdf) for context. Could you and legal provide a few concrete invoice examples and a short writeup we can share with our finance team?

Goal: get the examples by next Tuesday (03/30) so we can slot the pilot into our April run.

Best,
Elena
Procurement Manager, DataAxis

--
Attachment: DataAxis_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@dataaxis.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, kI <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-23T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot pricing questions — token accounting and minimums

Elena — thanks, great questions. I put together a short options document and three sample invoice scenarios (attached) to make this concrete. High level answers first:

- Long-context streaming: we meter on actual token consumption (input + output) at generation time, not a flat charge for the max context unless you pin a model/instance. For streaming, tokens emitted are billed as they are produced; large context windows only impact compute allocation/latency and may increase cost per token in practice (because of KV cache size), but we do not precharge the entire 40k unless you request pre-warming/reservation.

- Rounding & minimums: default quantum is 1,000 tokens for hosted usage on our standard SKU. That means any call that consumes 1–1,000 tokens will be rounded up to 1,000 for billing. For high-volume pilots we typically offer a committed-block model where quantum is effectively smoothed (committed block reduces per-token effective rate and removes the small-call rounding impact). Example: 120 calls * 90 tokens = 10,800 tokens billed as 12,000 in hosted-default (120 * 1,000) unless wrapped into a committed bucket or configured with a microfloor pilot waiver.

- Packaging options (we put three in the sheet):
  1) Pay-as-you-go (per-token) — fastest to start, subject to 1k quantum rounding.
  2) Committed monthly blocks (e.g., 2M tokens/month) — lower per-token, unused tokens roll into a 30-day buffer, rounding irrelevant inside the committed block.
  3) Hybrid seat + token credits — a small monthly seat + token pool for interactive users; recommended if you have steady seat-driven usage.

I attached pilot_pricing_options.xlsx and a sample_invoice_example.csv with concrete math for your 2M/month baseline under each option.

Proposed quick concession for pilots: 10% off committed-block list price + one-time 50k token onboarding credit to absorb initial experimental bursts. If that looks good, we can route a short SOW with those terms and include a DocuSign link.

Next steps: 1) check the math in the attached CSV, 2) tell me which packaging you prefer and whether procurement needs any legal exceptions on rounding, and 3) I'll loop in finance for the final pilot PO.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: pilot_pricing_options.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>; kI <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morris <elena.morris@dataaxis.com>
Date: 2027-03-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing questions — token accounting and minimums

Looping in briefly from pricing/legal:

- Legal: we can sign the pilot SOW with the 10% pilot discount and onboarding credit. For the rounding waiver: Legal will allow a one-time microfloor exception that applies for the pilot period only — specifically, override the 1k quantum for any usage below 150k total tokens in the first month; after that we revert to standard quantum unless you convert to a committed block. We need procurement to accept that clause in writing.

- Ops note (karthik): for very frequent microcalls we recommend enabling prefix caching and batching on your client side; that will materially reduce billed tokens and remove many of the tiny-call edgecases. I'll add a short config note to the shared Drive.

Vanessa
VP, Commercials — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@dataaxis.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataAxis Procurement <procurement@dataaxis.com>; vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-30T11:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing questions — token accounting and minimums

Priyom / Vanessa,

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from our finance team after reviewing the CSV:

1) The microfloor exception looks reasonable, but finance wants the example in your CSV to show net spend after the 50k onboarding credit and the 10% discount for committed-block option. Could you produce that adjusted sample?

2) Clarify streaming billing one more time: if input is 40k tokens and the model emits 2k tokens over the life of the request, will we be billed for 42k tokens or something higher because of internal KV/cache overhead? We need the worst-case net tokens figure to put in our forecast.

If you can update the sample invoice and confirm worst-case multiplier for KV overhead by end-of-day Friday (04/02), we can approve the pilot SOW and sign.

Best,
Elena

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@dataaxis.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai; kI <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot pricing questions — token accounting and minimums

Elena — thanks, attached is the updated sample_invoice_example.csv with the committed-block row showing the 10% discount and onboarding credit applied. Quick clarifications inline: 

- Net math: committed-block (2M tokens/month) @ list $0.0008/token -> $1,600 gross. With 10% pilot discount = $1,440. Subtract onboarding credit (50k tokens x $0.0008 = $40) applied month 1 -> $1,400 net invoice for month 1. I've included the month-1 and month-2 rows to show rollover behavior.

- Streaming + KV/cache overhead: billing is strictly input + output tokens. We do not bill an extra "KV token" metric. However, certain model runtimes can cause compute inefficiency (more GPU time) for large contexts; we factor that into the per-token price tiers for high-context SKUs. For hosted standard SKU, worst-case multiplier for tokens is ~1.03x (i.e., small accounting overhead <3%) purely for traceability and telemetry artifacts — not a separate line item on invoices. If you deploy a dedicated instance pinned to a model with 40k context, we can provide a fixed per-token rate that internally compensates for the overhead (and keeps your forecast stable).

Next steps: I will generate a short SOW with the pilot economics (10% off committed-block, 50k onboarding credit, and the one-time microfloor exception) and send a DocuSign link. Once signed we will provision the pilot and hand off to kI for the batching/prefix config.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/DocuSign-DX-SOW-089
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDA-DataAxis-Pilot

If that all looks good, please reply with an explicit acceptance of the microfloor clause and I'll route SOW.

Thanks,
Priyom
